prohibited_recommendations: Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD, NICE NG97 advises against it, and it may worsen behaviour.
Do not start memantine: a randomised trial showed no benefit in FTD and NICE NG97 advises against it.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
required_recommendations: Apply the Rascovsky 2011 criteria: state which features are present, the functional decline, and the level of certainty (possible or probable).

Explain why the escalating alcohol use (8 to 10 beers a day) does not account for the progressive frontal syndrome, and address it: a medically supervised reduction plan with withdrawal precautions, his wife controlling access, and oral thiamine.
Address safety and capacity: driving, finances (large unauthorised purchases; discuss lasting power of attorney), and the risk from his aggression to his wife and teenage son.
Arrange caregiver education and support, and a plan for behavioural symptoms that avoids cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine.
Offer genetic counselling before any genetic test, and discuss what a result would mean for relatives; predictive testing of his teenage son is deferred until adulthood.
Examine for motor neuron disease features (weakness, wasting, fasciculations, bulbar symptoms) at follow-up, since familial bvFTD can evolve into FTD with ALS.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not indicated in the standard FTD workup once a structural MRI and FDG-PET (or amyloid PET) have characterised the lobar pattern.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated without parkinsonism, and this examination shows normal tone and gait.

Familial frontotemporal dementia: diagno.summary: Rascovsky and colleagues (2011) define possible behavioural variant FTD by three of six behavioural and cognitive features, probable bvFTD by added functional decline and frontal or anterior temporal involvement on structural or functional imaging, and definite bvFTD by histopathology or a pathogenic mutation. C9orf72 expansions and GRN and MAPT variants cause most familial FTD; counselling precedes any genetic test and any predictive testing of relatives. Treatment is supportive: SSRIs or trazodone for behaviour, caregiver support and safety planning; cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are not recommended.

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. M. is a 53-year-old right-handed Hispanic man referred by his wife for progressive personality and behavioral changes over 2 years. She describes him as formerly highly motivated, organized, and ambitious. Two years ago, his behavior changed dramatically at work: he began making offensive comments to staff and customers, misappropriated cash from the register (which he denied), and was terminated after a customer altercation. At home, he has become increasingly impulsive — making large unauthorized purchases, getting into fights with neighbors, and ignoring personal hygiene. He eats voraciously, consuming all food in the refrigerator repeatedly. He insists on watching only boxing matches on television and becomes combative when interrupted. His alcohol consumption has escalated from occasional social use to 8-10 beers daily. He has no insight into any of these changes and reports feeling 'fine.' Family history is notable for his father, who had behavioral changes and dementia in his early 60s. Neurological review of systems negative.
